title: Ozone gave no clear repeated change in relative growth and development spread in North American and European papers from 1988-2015
abstract: We tested whether elevated ozone changed the relative spread of insect growth and development measures. We used 114 records from 24 papers in a public 2024 data release. The equal-paper coefficient-of-variation ratio was 1.042, with a conditional 95% interval of 0.919-1.181. All four North American and European region-period intervals included one after adjustment for four tests. The later European ratio was 1.473, but its adjusted interval was 0.902-2.405. Sample-size, endpoint-class and weighting checks did not establish a common increase. These results do not establish no effect. Paper dependence, mixed experimental units, reconstructed errors and selective reporting limit inference. The analysis does not test climate or weather interactions. The package contains code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and an external retrieval recipe.

display.caption: Exposed/control CV ratios in four region-period cells. Intervals have conditional family-wise 95 percent coverage under independent-paper t assumptions. One means no relative-spread change.
